points.quote: At Roehampton, assessments generally fall into one of three categories regarding AI. One, where no AI is possible or permitted; Two, where AI can be used as an assistive tool only; and three, where the use of AI is required to meet the design of the assessment.
points.gist: Roehampton assessments fall into three AI categories: no AI, AI as an assistive tool only, or AI required by the assessment design.

points.quote: Remember, only use AI if your assessment type allows it, or requires it. You must reference any use of AI.
points.gist: AI may be used only if the assessment type allows or requires it, and any use of AI must be referenced.

points.quote: You should check which AI rule-set applies to the assessment that you're working on.
points.gist: Students should check which of the University's AI rule-sets applies to the assessment they are working on.

points.quote: Use of AI is not allowed
points.gist: Type 1 assessments do not allow use of AI.

points.quote: An in person presentation or oral report
points.gist: An in-person presentation or oral report is given as a Type 1 example.

points.quote: AI can be used as an assistive tool only
points.gist: In Type 2 assessments AI can be used as an assistive tool only.

points.quote: A written assignment where AI was used to proofread a draft
points.gist: Using AI to proofread a draft of a written assignment is a Type 2 example.
In Type 3 assessments use of AI is mandatory.

points.quote: A reflective essay in which students critique AI output
points.gist: A reflective essay critiquing AI output is given as a Type 3 example.

points.quote: You should not copy and paste from an AI tool.
points.gist: Students should not copy and paste from an AI tool.

points.quote: You should turn off the tool’s ability to learn on your data, this means your information is not used to train AI.
points.anchor: Using AI for Coding and Maths
points.gist: When using AI for data analysis, turn off the tool's ability to learn on your data so it is not used for training.

points.quote: To safeguard your information, avoid sharing any personal or confidential data with AI systems. Always anonymise datasets, and limit access to only trusted platforms.
points.anchor: Using AI for Coding and Maths
points.gist: Avoid sharing personal or confidential data with AI systems; always anonymise datasets and limit access to trusted platforms.

points.quote: Have I fact checked everything? AI will sometimes produce factually inaccurate information such as fabricated sources.
points.gist: Students should fact check everything, since AI sometimes produces inaccurate information such as fabricated sources.

points.quote: Ensure that you are using AI to support rather than replace your own thinking.
points.gist: Students should use AI to support rather than replace their own thinking.
